\section[el experimento]{el experimento — the experiment}

\label{lesson:ES-C599-experimento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to make an effort, then the Spanish for to contribute.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el experimento}
\textbf{el experimento} — \textquotedblleft{}the experiment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Hicimos un experimento en clase.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We did an experiment in class.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Hacer un experimento} — to do an experiment.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{experimento} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{experimentum} 'a test, a trial', built on \emph{experiri} 'to try out' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el experimento}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el experimento}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el experimento}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to make an effort, then the Spanish for to contribute, then say \emph{el experimento} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el experimento mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The experiment\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[comparar]{comparar — to compare}

\label{lesson:ES-C599-comparar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to contribute, then the Spanish for the experiment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: comparar}
\textbf{comparar} — \textquotedblleft{}to compare\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Comparamos los resultados de dos grupos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We compared the results of two groups.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Comparar con} — to compare with.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{comparar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{comparare} 'to put together, to match', built on \emph{par} 'equal' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{comparar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{comparar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to contribute, then the Spanish for the experiment, then say \emph{comparar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\end{tcolorbox}
\section[analizar]{analizar — to analyse}

\label{lesson:ES-C599-analizar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the experiment, then the Spanish for to compare.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: analizar}
\textbf{analizar} — \textquotedblleft{}to analyse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Tenemos que analizar los datos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We have to analyse the data.}
\end{quote}

Spelling: \emph{analicé}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{analizar} is built on \emph{análisis}, a learned borrowing from Greek \emph{analysis} 'a loosening, a breaking up' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la conclusión]{la conclusión — the conclusion}

\label{lesson:ES-C599-conclusion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to compare, then the Spanish for to analyse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la conclusión}
\textbf{la conclusión} — \textquotedblleft{}the conclusion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Llegamos a una conclusión.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We reached a conclusion.}
\end{quote}

\emph{En conclusión} — in conclusion.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{conclusión} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{conclusio} 'a closing, an end', built on \emph{concludere} and \emph{claudere} 'to shut' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la conclusión}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to compare, then the Spanish for to analyse, then say \emph{la conclusión} again
\end{itemize}

\section[el método]{el método — the method}

\label{lesson:ES-C599-metodo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to analyse, then the Spanish for the conclusion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el método}
\textbf{el método} — \textquotedblleft{}the method\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Es un buen método para estudiar.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It is a good method for studying.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Método de pago} — payment method.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{método} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{methodus}, taken from Greek \emph{methodos} 'a following after, a way of inquiry', built from \emph{meta} and \emph{hodos} 'way' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el método}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el método}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el método}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to analyse, then the Spanish for the conclusion, then say \emph{el método} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el método mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The method\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[(dialogue)]{Repaso de los capítulos 592–599}

\label{lesson:ES-R599-repaso-592-599}



\begin{quote}
Say the Spanish for the businessman and the multinational company.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item the businessman, the multinational company, the industry, the head office, the branch
  \item the task, to carry out, the performance, to do for a living, efficient
  \item the leadership, to motivate, the collaboration, to run, to manage
  \item the career, to be promoted, the merit, ambitious, to succeed
  \item the syllabus, the enrolment, the tutorial, the faculty, the master's degree
  \item the learning, the teaching, to educate, to assess, the assessment
  \item the knowledge, the skill, the ability, to make an effort, to contribute
  \item the experiment, to compare, to analyse, the conclusion, the method
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The businessman? (\textbf{el empresario}.) The multinational company? (\textbf{la multinacional}.) The industry? (\textbf{la industria}.) The head office? (\textbf{la sede}.) The branch? (\textbf{la sucursal}.) The task? (\textbf{la tarea}.) To carry out? (\textbf{desempeñar}.) The performance? (\textbf{el rendimiento}.) To do for a living? (\textbf{dedicarse}.) Efficient? (\textbf{eficiente}.) The leadership? (\textbf{el liderazgo}.) To motivate? (\textbf{motivar}.) The collaboration? (\textbf{la colaboración}.) To run? (\textbf{dirigir}.) To manage? (\textbf{gestionar}.) The career? (\textbf{la carrera}.) To be promoted? (\textbf{ascender}.) The merit? (\textbf{el mérito}.) Ambitious? (\textbf{ambicioso}.) To succeed? (\textbf{triunfar}.) The syllabus? (\textbf{el temario}.) The enrolment? (\textbf{la matrícula}.) The tutorial? (\textbf{la tutoría}.) The faculty? (\textbf{la facultad}.) The master's degree? (\textbf{el máster}.) The learning? (\textbf{el aprendizaje}.) The teaching? (\textbf{la enseñanza}.) To educate? (\textbf{educar}.) To assess? (\textbf{evaluar}.) The assessment? (\textbf{la evaluación}.) The knowledge? (\textbf{el conocimiento}.) The skill? (\textbf{la habilidad}.) The ability? (\textbf{la capacidad}.) To make an effort? (\textbf{esforzarse}.) To contribute? (\textbf{aportar}.) The experiment? (\textbf{el experimento}.) To compare? (\textbf{comparar}.) To analyse? (\textbf{analizar}.) The conclusion? (\textbf{la conclusión}.) The method? (\textbf{el método}.)
